records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse an array in place
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of size N, reverse the array in-place so that the first element becomes the last, the second becomes second-to-last, and so on.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^6, -10^9 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Space Complexity: O(1). Time Complexity: O(N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set left = 0 and right = n - 1. While left < right, swap arr[left] and arr[right], then move both pointers inward. Return arr.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the second largest and second smallest elements in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of N integers, find the second largest and second smallest elements. If no such element exists, return -1.
records.constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 10^6, -10^9 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(N) single pass.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize smallest, secondSmallest, largest, secondLargest. Scan once; update these four values whenever a smaller/larger distinct value is found. Return the two second values, or -1 when they do not exist.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Move all zeros to the end while preserving the relative order of other elements
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of N integers, move all 0s to the end of the array while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements in-place.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set write = 0. Scan the array; whenever arr[i] is non-zero, swap arr[i] with arr[write] and increment write. Remaining positions naturally contain zero.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the missing number in an array of n distinct values from 0 to n
records.problem_statement: Given an array nums containing N distinct numbers in the range [0, N], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^6, 0 \le nums[i] \le N. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set answer = 0. XOR answer with every value from 0..N and every value in nums. The duplicate values cancel and the remaining XOR is the missing number.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the single non-repeating element where every other element appears twice
records.problem_statement: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single element.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 3 \cdot 10^4, -3 \cdot 10^4 \le nums[i] \le 3 \cdot 10^4. Time Complexity: O(N), Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set answer = 0. XOR answer with every array element. Equal pairs cancel, leaving the unique element.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum subarray sum (Kadane's Algorithm)
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set current = nums[0], best = nums[0]. For each later value x, set current = max(x, current + x), then best = max(best, current). Return best.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum product subarray
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, find a contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product, and return the product.
records.solution_pseudocode: Track maxEnding and minEnding because a negative value can swap them. For each x, compute the three candidates x, x*maxEnding, x*minEnding; update both extremes and the global maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the "leaders" in an array — elements greater than everything to their right
records.problem_statement: Given an array A of positive integers, find all the leaders in the array. An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan from right to left, keep maxRight, and collect any value strictly greater than maxRight. Reverse the collected list before returning.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rearrange an array so positive and negative numbers alternate
records.problem_statement: Given an array of positive and negative integers, rearrange them in alternating order such that every positive number is followed by a negative number, maintaining relative order where possible.
records.solution_pseudocode: Partition values into positive and negative positions while preserving order as required. Use two sequences or stable placement pointers, then interleave positive and negative values until one side is exhausted.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rotate an array to the right by k positions in O(1) extra space
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative, in-place.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set k = k mod n. Reverse the whole array, reverse the first k elements, then reverse the remaining elements. Return the rotated array.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the equilibrium index of an array (left sum equals right sum)
records.problem_statement: An equilibrium index of an array is an index such that the sum of elements at lower indices is equal to the sum of elements at higher indices. Return the first equilibrium index or -1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute total sum. Keep leftSum = 0. For each index i, subtract arr[i] from total to obtain rightSum; if leftSum equals rightSum, return i. Then add arr[i] to leftSum. Return -1.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the majority element appearing more than n/2 times (Boyer–Moore Voting)
records.problem_statement: Given an array nums of size N, return the majority element that appears more than \lfloor N/2 \rfloor times.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 5 \cdot 10^4, -10^9 \le nums[i] \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(N), Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use Boyer-Moore voting: maintain candidate and count. Increase count for the candidate, decrease for different values, and replace candidate when count reaches zero. Optionally verify the candidate count at the end.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all Pythagorean triplets in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers, write a function that returns true if there is a triplet (a, b, c) that satisfies a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
records.solution_pseudocode: Square every value and store or sort the squares. For each possible largest square c2, use two pointers on the smaller squares to test whether a2 + b2 = c2.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Merge two sorted arrays in place without extra space
records.problem_statement: Given two sorted arrays arr1 of size M and arr2 of size N, merge them in-place such that arr1 contains the first M smallest elements and arr2 contains the remaining N elements, both sorted.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le M, N \le 5 \cdot 10^4, 0 \le arr1[i], arr2[j] \le 10^9. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use the gap method: treat both arrays as one virtual array. Compare elements gap positions apart, swap when out of order, and reduce the gap until it becomes zero.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the union and intersection of two arrays
records.problem_statement: Given two unsorted/sorted arrays, find the count and elements representing their union (distinct elements from both) and intersection (common elements).
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert elements from both arrays into a set for the union. Build a frequency/set representation and collect elements present in both inputs for the intersection.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find a pair with a given sum in an unsorted array (Two Sum)
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
records.constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 10^4, -10^9 \le nums[i], target \le 10^9. Exactly one solution exists.
records.solution_pseudocode: Create a hash map from value to index. For each nums[i], compute need = target - nums[i]; if need exists, return its stored index and i. Otherwise store nums[i].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find a contiguous subarray with a given sum in a non-negative array
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of non-negative integers and an integer sum, find a contiguous subarray that adds to the given sum. Return 1-based start and end indices.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a sliding window because all values are non-negative. Expand the right end and add to sum. While sum exceeds target, move left and subtract. When sum equals target, return the indices.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Sort an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s in one pass (Dutch National Flag)
records.problem_statement: Given an array nums with N objects colored red, white, or blue (represented as 0, 1, 2), sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^6, nums[i] \in \\{0, 1, 2\\}. Single pass O(N), Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain low, mid, high. While mid <= high: if value is 0 swap with low and advance low/mid; if 1 advance mid; if 2 swap with high and decrement high.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of platforms needed given arrival and departure times
records.problem_statement: Given arrival and departure times of all trains that reach a railway station, find the minimum number of platforms required for the station so that no train waits.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort arrival and departure times. Use two pointers i,j and current platforms. If the next arrival is before/equal to the next departure, increment platforms and i; otherwise decrement platforms and advance j. Track the maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Maximize the sum of i × arr[i] achievable by rotating an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of N integers, find the maximum value of \sum\_{i=0}^{N-1} i \cdot arr[i] among all possible rotations of the array.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute the initial weighted sum S = sum(i * arr[i]) and total sum. For each rotation, update S = S + totalSum - n * movedElement. Track the maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Trapping Rain Water — compute total water trapped between bars
records.problem_statement: Given N non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use left and right pointers with leftMax and rightMax. Move the side with the smaller height; trapped water on that side is maxSoFar - currentHeight. Accumulate the total.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the next permutation of a given array
records.problem_statement: Rearrange numbers into the lexicographically next greater permutation of numbers. If such an arrangement is impossible, rearrange it as the lowest possible order (sorted in ascending order).
records.solution_pseudocode: Find the longest non-increasing suffix. Let i be the pivot before it. If a pivot exists, find the rightmost value greater than arr[i] and swap them. Reverse the suffix. This gives the next lexicographic permutation.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rotate a square matrix by 90 degrees in place
records.problem_statement: You are given an N \times N 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise) in-place.
records.solution_pseudocode: Transpose the matrix in place, then reverse every row. The result is the matrix rotated 90 degrees clockwise.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print a matrix in spiral order
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order (outer border clockwise inward).
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain top, bottom, left, right boundaries. Traverse top row, right column, bottom row, and left column while shrinking the boundaries. Append visited elements in order.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Search a target in a matrix sorted row-wise and column-wise
records.problem_statement: Write an efficient algorithm that searches for a value target in an M \times N integer matrix where integers in each row and column are sorted in ascending order.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le M, N \le 300, -10^9 \le matrix[i][j], target \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(M + N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Start at the top-right corner. If current equals target, return it. If current > target move left; otherwise move down. Stop when outside the matrix.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: If an element in a matrix is zero, set its entire row and column to zero, in place
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N integer matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0s in-place.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le M, N \le 200, -2^{31} \le matrix[i][j] \le 2^{31} - 1. Auxiliary Space: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use the first row and first column as markers. Record whether the first row/column originally contained zero. Mark rows and columns when a zero is found, then zero marked rows/columns.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the row with the maximum number of 1s in a boolean matrix sorted row-wise
records.problem_statement: Given a boolean 2D array of size N \times M where each row is sorted, find the 0-indexed row that has the maximum number of 1s.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N, M \le 1000, matrix[i][j] \in \\{0, 1\\}. Time Complexity: O(N + M).
records.solution_pseudocode: Start from the top-right. Move left while values are 1 and update the best row; when value is 0 move down. The sorted rows make this O(rows + cols).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest consecutive sequence of elements in an unsorted array
records.problem_statement: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence a, a+1, a+2, \dots.
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert all numbers into a set. For each value x that has no predecessor x-1, repeatedly count x, x+1, ... until the sequence ends. Track the maximum length.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the end of an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array of non-negative integers nums, you are initially positioned at the first index. Each element represents your maximum jump length at that position. Return minimum jumps to reach the last index.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain farthest reachable index and current range end. When i reaches currentEnd, increment jumps and set currentEnd to farthest. Return jumps when the last index becomes reachable.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a string is a palindrome, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set left = 0 and right = n - 1. Skip non-alphanumeric characters and compare case-insensitively. If any pair differs return false; otherwise return true.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether two strings are anagrams of each other
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise (same character counts).
records.solution_pseudocode: Count each character in the first string and decrement counts while scanning the second. If lengths differ or any count becomes negative, return false; otherwise true.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse the words in a sentence without using a built-in reverse function
records.problem_statement: Given an input string s, reverse the order of the words. Words are separated by at least one space. Return string with single spaces between words.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le |s| \le 10^4. Auxiliary Space: O(1) extra memory where applicable.
records.solution_pseudocode: Split the sentence into words, then read the word list from end to start and append each word to the result with single spaces.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the first non-repeating character in a string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, find the first non-repeating character in it and return its index. If it does not exist, return -1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count character frequencies in one pass. Scan the string again and return the first character whose count is one; otherwise return the failure value.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement run-length compression (e.g. "aabcccccaaa" → "a2b1c5a3")
records.problem_statement: Perform basic string compression using the counts of repeated characters. If compressed string is not smaller than original, return original.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan consecutive equal characters with a count. Append each character followed by its run length when the run ends.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether one string is a rotation of another
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s and goal, return true if and only if s can become goal after some number of shifts on s.
records.solution_pseudocode: If lengths differ return false. Check whether s2 occurs inside s1 concatenated with itself.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest palindromic substring in a string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.
records.solution_pseudocode: For every index, expand around it as a center for odd-length and even-length palindromes. Track the longest interval found.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest common prefix among an array of strings
records.problem_statement: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. Return "" if no common prefix exists.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use the first string as the candidate prefix. Compare it with each other string and shorten the prefix until it matches the beginning of the current string.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a string's characters can be rearranged into a palindrome
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, determine if a permutation of the string could form a palindrome.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count character frequencies. At most one character may have an odd frequency. Return true when that condition holds.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement your own substring search (like strstr()/indexOf()) without built-ins
records.problem_statement: Given two strings haystack and needle, return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if needle is not part of haystack.
records.solution_pseudocode: For every starting position in the text, compare pattern characters one by one. If all match, return the position. If none match, return -1.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all permutations of a given string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, print/return all unique permutations of the string in lexicographical order.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use backtracking. At each position choose an unused character, place it, recurse to the next position, then undo the choice. Record complete strings.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether two strings are exactly one edit apart
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, determine if they are both one edit distance apart (insert, delete, or replace a single character).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use two pointers. If characters differ, allow exactly one operation: replace when lengths match, otherwise advance only the longer string pointer for insert/delete. Reject a second difference.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum edits (insert/delete/replace) to convert one string into another (Edit Distance)
records.problem_statement: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2 (insert, delete, replace).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the minimum edits to transform the first i characters of A into the first j of B. Match characters diagonally; otherwise take 1 + min(delete, insert, replace).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Group a list of strings into anagram groups
records.problem_statement: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
records.solution_pseudocode: For each word, sort its characters or compute a frequency signature. Use the signature as a hash-map key and append the word to that group.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest substring without repeating characters
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a sliding window with lastSeen positions. Expand right; when a repeated character is inside the window, move left past its previous position. Track maximum window length.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement basic wildcard pattern matching with '.' and '\*'
records.problem_statement: Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement wildcard pattern matching where . matches any single character and * matches zero or more of any sequence.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP or greedy matching with backtracking at wildcard *. A dot matches any one character and * can match zero or more of the preceding token. Return whether the entire text matches.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Convert a Roman numeral to an integer, and vice versa
records.problem_statement: Write two functions: one to convert a Roman numeral string to an integer, and another to convert an integer (1 to 3999) to a Roman numeral.
records.solution_pseudocode: For Roman-to-integer, scan left to right and subtract a value when it is smaller than the next; otherwise add. For integer-to-Roman, repeatedly append the largest possible symbol value.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum window substring of one string containing all characters of another
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le m, n \le 10^5. Time Complexity: O(m + n).
records.solution_pseudocode: Count required characters. Expand right until all requirements are satisfied. Then shrink left while the window remains valid, recording the shortest valid window.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count and generate all valid IP addresses that can be formed from a digit string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s containing only digits, return all possible valid IPv4 addresses that can be formed by inserting dots.
records.solution_pseudocode: Backtrack over positions, choosing 1 to 3 digits per segment. Reject leading zeros and values above 255. When 4 segments consume the entire string, record the address.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement atoi() — convert a string to an integer, handling edge cases
records.problem_statement: Implement myAtoi(string s) which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer handling leading spaces, signs (+/-), non-digit characters, and 32-bit overflow thresholds [-2^{31}, 2^{31}-1].
records.solution_pseudocode: Skip leading spaces, read optional sign, then consume digits while building the number. Before multiplying by 10, check for 32-bit overflow and clamp if necessary.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings
records.problem_statement: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the LCS length of prefixes. If characters match, use 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise use max of the top and left cells.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a string follows a given word pattern
records.problem_statement: Given a pattern and a string s, find if s follows the same pattern (a bijection between a letter in pattern and a non-empty word in s).
records.solution_pseudocode: Split s into words. Maintain a bijection: each pattern character maps to one word and each word maps to one character. Return true only when all mappings are consistent.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the smallest window in a string containing all its own distinct characters
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, find the smallest window length containing all the distinct characters of the given string itself.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count the number of distinct characters in the whole string. Use a sliding window and maintain distinct characters present; shrink from the left while the window still contains all required characters.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Given a dictionary, determine whether a string can be segmented into dictionary words (Word Break)
records.problem_statement: Given a string s and a dictionary of strings wordDict, return true if s can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use dp[i] = true when prefix s[0:i] can be segmented. For each i, test every prior split j and set dp[i] if dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is in the dictionary.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find a pair in a sorted array that sums to a target value
records.problem_statement: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers numbers and a target, find two numbers such that they add up to target.
records.constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 3 \cdot 10^4, -1000 \le numbers[i], target \le 1000. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set left = 0 and right = n - 1. If numbers[left] + numbers[right] equals target, return them. If the sum is too small move left; otherwise move right.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the container that holds the most water, given an array of heights
records.problem_statement: Given n non-negative integers a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n representing lines at index i, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container containing the most water.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use two pointers at both ends. Compute area = min(height[left], height[right]) * (right-left). Move the pointer at the smaller height inward and keep the maximum area.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all unique triplets in an array that sum to zero (3Sum)
records.problem_statement:
Given an integer array nums, return all the unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i 
eq j, i 
eq k, j 
eq k and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort nums. For each i, use two pointers left/right to find pairs summing to -nums[i]. Skip duplicates for i, left, and right to keep only unique triplets.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place, returning the new length
records.problem_statement: Given a sorted array nums, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. Return the new size.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use write = 1. Scan from the second element; when nums[i] differs from nums[write-1], copy it to nums[write] and increment write. Return write.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest substring with at most k distinct characters
records.problem_statement: Given a string s and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring of s that contains at most k distinct characters.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a sliding window and a frequency map. Expand right; while distinct count exceeds k, remove from the left. Track the maximum window length.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of size k
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers arr and a number k, find the maximum sum of a subarray of size k.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le k \le N \le 10^6, -10^5 \le arr[i] \le 10^5. Time Complexity: O(N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute the sum of the first k elements. Slide the window by subtracting the outgoing value and adding the incoming value. Track the largest sum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the smallest subarray with a sum ≥ a given value
records.problem_statement: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target, return the minimal length of a contiguous subarray of which the sum is greater than or equal to target. If none exists, return 0.
records.solution_pseudocode: Expand right and add values to sum. While sum >= target, update the minimum length and remove arr[left] before incrementing left.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Merge all overlapping intervals in a list
records.problem_statement: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort intervals by start. Start with the first interval; if the next start is <= current end, extend current end. Otherwise append current interval and start a new one.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all starting indices of a pattern's anagrams within a string
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count characters of the pattern. Maintain a fixed-size sliding window of the same length in the text and compare frequency counts; record every matching window start.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rearrange an array into a "wiggle" pattern where every even-indexed element is less than its neighbors
records.problem_statement: Given an unsorted array nums, reorder it in-place such that nums[0] \le nums[1] \ge nums[2] \le nums[3] \dots
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan adjacent pairs. At even index require a[i] <= a[i+1]; at odd index require a[i] >= a[i+1]. Swap each violating pair.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Binary Search on a sorted array, iteratively and recursively
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, search target in nums. Return index or -1.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, -10^9 \le target, nums[i] \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(\log N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set low = 0 and high = n - 1. Repeatedly compute mid. If a[mid] equals target return it; if smaller search right half; otherwise search left half. For recursion, call the same logic on the selected half.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Search for a target in a rotated sorted array
records.problem_statement: Given array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values) that has been rotated at an unknown pivot, find target index in O(\log N) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use binary search. At each step determine which half is sorted. If target lies inside the sorted half, search it; otherwise search the other half.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the first and last occurrence of a target value in a sorted array
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given target value in O(\log N) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Run binary search twice: once biased left to find the first occurrence and once biased right to find the last occurrence.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the integer square root of a number using binary search
records.problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer x, compute and return the square root of x truncated to the nearest integer (\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor).
records.solution_pseudocode: Binary-search x in [0, n]. Keep the largest mid with mid*mid <= n and return it.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find a peak element in an array (greater than both neighbors)
records.problem_statement: A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. Find a peak element and return its index in O(\log N) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Binary-search on slopes. If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], move right; otherwise move left including mid. The remaining index is a peak.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Bubble, Selection, and Insertion Sort, and state their time complexities
records.problem_statement: Implement the three elementary sorting algorithms for an array of N integers and output the sorted array.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 1000, -10^4 \le arr[i] \le 10^4. Time Complexity: O(N^2), Space: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Bubble: repeatedly swap adjacent inversions. Selection: find the minimum remaining value and place it at the current position. Insertion: shift larger sorted-prefix values right and insert the current value.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Merge Sort and explain why it's stable and O(n log n) in every case
records.problem_statement: Implement the divide-and-conquer Merge Sort algorithm to sort an array in non-decreasing order.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively split the array into halves until one element remains. Merge two sorted halves with two pointers into a temporary array. Copy back. Equal values are taken from the left first, preserving stability.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Quick Sort and explain how pivot choice affects worst-case behavior
records.problem_statement: Implement Quick Sort using the Partition procedure (e.g. Lomuto or Hoare) to sort an array.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, -10^9 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Average Time Complexity: O(N \log N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Choose a pivot, partition the array into values less than/greater than the pivot, then recursively sort both sides. Randomized or median-like pivots reduce the chance of worst-case partitions.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Counting Sort and explain when it beats comparison-based sorts
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr where elements are in a known range [0, K], sort the array in linear time using Counting Sort.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^6, 0 \le arr[i] \le K \le 10^6. Time Complexity: O(N + K), Space: O(K).
records.solution_pseudocode: Find min and max. Create a count array for the value range, accumulate counts into positions, and place each item into the output. Use it when the value range K is reasonably small compared with N.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the Kth smallest/largest element without fully sorting the array
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k^{\text{th}} largest element in the array using QuickSelect or Min-Heap.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use QuickSelect: partition around a pivot and recurse only into the side containing index k. Stop when the pivot lands at the target index.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(min(m,n))) time
records.problem_statement: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size M and N, return the median of the two sorted arrays.
records.constraints_text: 0 \le M, N \le 1000, 1 \le M + N \le 2000, -10^6 \le nums1[i], nums2[i] \le 10^6.
records.solution_pseudocode: Binary-search the smaller array for a partition where all left-side elements are <= all right-side elements. Check partition boundaries and compute the median from the largest left and smallest right values.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Sort a "nearly sorted" array where each element is misplaced by at most k
records.problem_statement: Given an array of N elements, where each element is at most k positions away from its target position in the sorted array, sort the array efficiently using Min-Heap.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, 1 \le k < N. Time Complexity: O(N \log k).
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert the first k+1 elements into a min-heap. Repeatedly extract the minimum to the output and insert the next array element. Continue until the heap is empty.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count the number of inversions in an array (pairs where a[i] > a[j] for i < j)
records.problem_statement: Inversion Count for an array indicates how far (or close) the array is from being sorted. Two elements a[i] and a[j] form an inversion if a[i] > a[j] and i < j.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, 1 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(N \log N) via modified Merge Sort.
records.solution_pseudocode: During merge sort, when a right-half value is smaller than a left-half value, add the number of remaining left elements to the inversion count. Merge normally.
records.time_complexity: O(N \log N) via modified Merge Sort

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the majority element that appears more than n/3 times
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array of size N, find all elements that appear more than \lfloor N/3 \rfloor times using Extended Boyer-Moore Voting algorithm.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 5 \cdot 10^4, -10^9 \le nums[i] \le 10^9. Time Complexity: O(N), Space: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain two candidates and counters using extended Boyer-Moore voting. After the scan, verify both candidates and return those whose frequency exceeds n/3.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse a singly linked list, iteratively and recursively
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
records.solution_pseudocode: Iteratively, keep prev = null and curr = head; save next, reverse curr.next to prev, then advance. Return prev. Recursively, reverse the suffix and point the next node back to curr.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Detect a cycle in a linked list and find where it begins (Floyd's algorithm)
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return null.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [0, 10^4], -10^5 \le Node.val \le 10^5. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Move slow by one and fast by two until they meet or fast reaches null. If they meet, reset one pointer to head and advance both one step; their meeting point is the cycle start.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the middle node of a linked list in a single pass
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node. If there are two middle nodes, return the second middle node.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 100]. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Move slow one step and fast two steps. When fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle node.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list
records.problem_statement: Merge two sorted linked lists and return it as a sorted list by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in both lists in [0, 50], -100 \le Node.val \le 100.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a dummy node and a tail pointer. Repeatedly append the smaller current node from the two lists, then append the remaining list.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Remove the Nth node from the end of a linked list in one pass
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, remove the N^{\text{th}} node from the end of the list and return its head.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes SZ \in [1, 30], 1 \le N \le SZ. Single pass O(1) extra space.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use two pointers with a dummy node. Move fast n steps ahead, then advance fast and slow together until fast reaches the end. Remove slow.next.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a linked list is a palindrome
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return true if it is a palindrome or false otherwise.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 10^5], 0 \le Node.val \le 9. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half, then compare nodes from both halves. Return true if all values match.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the intersection point of two linked lists
records.problem_statement: Given the heads of two singly linked lists headA and headB, return the node at which the two lists intersect. If no intersection, return null.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 3 \cdot 10^4]. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Set pointers p=headA and q=headB. When p reaches null switch it to headB; when q reaches null switch it to headA. They meet at the intersection or null.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Remove duplicates from an unsorted linked list
records.problem_statement: Write code to remove duplicates from an unsorted linked list.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 10^4], -10^4 \le Node.val \le 10^4. Time: O(N), Space: O(N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Traverse with a previous pointer and a hash set. If current value is already in the set, bypass current; otherwise add the value and advance.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Add two numbers represented as linked lists with digits in reverse order
records.problem_statement: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. Digits are stored in reverse order. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list.
records.solution_pseudocode: Traverse both lists with carry. At each step compute sum = a + b + carry, create a node with sum mod 10, and update carry = sum / 10.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse a linked list in groups of size k
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time, and return the modified list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k, leave left-out nodes as is.
records.solution_pseudocode: Check whether at least k nodes remain. Reverse exactly k nodes, recursively process the remainder, and connect the reversed block to the returned suffix.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rotate a linked list to the right by k places
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, rotate the list to the right by k places.
records.solution_pseudocode: Find length and tail, connect tail to head to form a cycle, compute the new tail at n - (k mod n) - 1, break the cycle, and return the new head.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Flatten a multilevel linked list where nodes may have a child pointer
records.problem_statement: You are given a doubly linked list, where in addition to next/prev pointers, each node has a child pointer. Flatten the list so all nodes appear in a single-level doubly linked list.
records.solution_pseudocode: Traverse the main list. When a node has a child, recursively flatten that child list, insert it immediately after the node, then reconnect the original next list after the flattened child.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Clone a linked list that has random pointers (deep copy)
records.problem_statement: A linked list of length N is given where each node contains an additional random pointer which could point to any node in the list or null. Construct a deep copy of the list.
records.solution_pseudocode: Create a clone node for every original node and store original->clone in a map. Traverse again to assign next and random pointers using the map.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Sort a linked list using merge sort
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, return the list after sorting it in ascending order in O(N \log N) time and O(\log N) space.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively split the array into halves until one element remains. Merge two sorted halves with two pointers into a temporary array. Copy back. Equal values are taken from the left first, preserving stability.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Convert a sorted linked list into a height-balanced BST
records.problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list where elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use slow/fast pointers to find the middle node as root. Recursively build the left subtree from the left half and the right subtree from the right half.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a doubly linked list with insert, delete, and traverse
records.problem_statement: Design and implement a Doubly Linked List class supporting insertAtHead, insertAtTail, deleteNode, and forward/backward traversal.
records.constraints_text: Operations count up to 10^5. Time per operation O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain head/tail and prev/next links. For insertion update neighboring pointers in O(1); for deletion reconnect previous and next nodes; traverse forward or backward as requested.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a circular linked list and detect whether a list is circular
records.problem_statement: Implement insertion and deletion in a Circular Linked List and write a function isCircular(head) that returns true if the list loops back to the head node.
records.solution_pseudocode: For insertion/deletion, preserve the circular next links and head/tail references. To test circularity, follow next pointers and check whether traversal returns to head before reaching null.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Swap every two adjacent nodes in a linked list without swapping values
records.problem_statement: Given a linked list, swap every two adjacent nodes and return its head. You must solve the problem without modifying the values in the list's nodes (only node links can be changed).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a dummy node before the head. For each pair, set first.next to second.next, second.next to first, and connect the previous pair to second.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find and remove the loop in a linked list
records.problem_statement: Given a linked list that may contain a loop, detect if a loop exists and break/remove the loop so that the last node points to null.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 10^5]. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use Floyd to detect the cycle. After finding the cycle start, walk another pointer around the cycle until its next is the start, then set that next pointer to null.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether an expression has balanced parentheses using a stack
records.problem_statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
records.solution_pseudocode: Push opening brackets onto a stack. For a closing bracket, verify the stack is non-empty and its top matches; otherwise return false. At the end the stack must be empty.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a queue using two stacks, and a stack using two queues
records.problem_statement: Implement a First In First Out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks, and a Last In First Out (LIFO) stack using two queues. All operations (push, pop, peek, empty) must function correctly.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain inputStack and outputStack. Push into input. For pop/peek, if output is empty move all items from input to output, then use output for the operation.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Design a stack that retrieves the minimum element in O(1) time
records.problem_statement: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element (getMin) in O(1) constant time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use one normal stack and one min stack. On push also push the current minimum to minStack; on pop remove from both. getMin returns minStack.top.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the next greater element for every element in an array using a stack
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr, for each element find the first element to its right that is strictly greater. If no such element exists, output -1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan from right to left with a monotonic decreasing stack. Pop values <= current; the remaining top is the next greater element, then push current.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Evaluate a postfix (Reverse Polish Notation) expression
records.problem_statement: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation. Valid operators are +, -, *, /.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan tokens. Push numbers. For an operator, pop right operand then left operand, apply the operator, and push the result. The final stack value is the answer.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Convert an infix expression to postfix using a stack
records.problem_statement: Given an infix expression containing operands, binary operators (+, -, *, /, ^), and parentheses, convert it to Postfix notation (Shunting-yard algorithm).
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan tokens. Push numbers. For an operator, pop right operand then left operand, apply the operator, and push the result. The final stack value is the answer.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a circular queue backed by a fixed-size array
records.problem_statement: Design your implementation of the circular queue. The circular queue is a linear data structure in which the operations are performed based on FIFO principle and the last position is connected back to the first.
records.solution_pseudocode: Store elements in a fixed array with front, rear and size. Enqueue at rear = (rear+1) mod capacity; dequeue at front = (front+1) mod capacity.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Design and implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache
records.problem_statement: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with get(key) and put(key, value) in O(1) time complexity.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a hash map plus doubly linked list. Map keys to nodes; move every accessed or inserted node to the front. When capacity is exceeded, remove the least recently used node at the tail.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the largest rectangular area in a histogram using a stack
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a monotonic increasing stack of indices. When the current height is smaller, pop bars and compute each popped bar area using the current index as the right boundary and the new stack top as the left boundary.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a stack supporting push, pop, and getMax() all in O(1)
records.problem_statement: Design a custom stack structure that supports push(x), pop(), top(), and getMax() operations, all operating in O(1) time complexity.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain a normal stack and an auxiliary max stack. Push the larger of the new value and current maximum to maxStack. Pop both together; getMax reads maxStack.top.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Sort a stack using only stack operations, no extra array
records.problem_statement: Given a stack, sort it such that top contains the maximum element. You may only use another temporary stack and standard operations (push, pop, peek, isEmpty).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a temporary stack. Pop items from the input; move larger items back to the input until the correct position is found, then push the item into the temporary stack. Transfer back when done.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum in every sliding window of size k using a deque
records.problem_statement: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k moving from left to right. Return the max sliding window elements.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, 1 \le k \le N. Time Complexity: O(N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain a deque of indices whose values are decreasing. Remove indices outside the window and smaller values from the back. The front always holds the maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Design a queue supporting getFront, getRear, and peek in O(1)
records.problem_statement: Implement a Double Ended Queue (Deque) or standard queue class supporting O(1) access to front and rear elements without built-in library structures.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain front and rear pointers (or a deque). Insert/remove at the respective end and update pointers so front/rear access stays O(1).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a basic calculator that evaluates +, -, \*, /, and parentheses from a string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s representing a valid expression, evaluate this expression and return the result.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan the expression while tracking current number, sign, and a running result. Use a stack to save result and sign before '('; on ')' combine the current subexpression with the saved state.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Given a sequence of pushed and popped values, check whether it's a valid stack sequence
records.problem_statement: Given two integer arrays pushed and popped each with distinct values, return true if this could have been the result of a sequence of push and pop operations on an initially empty stack.
records.solution_pseudocode: Simulate pushes into a stack. After each push, while the stack top equals the next required popped value, pop it. At the end, the popped sequence is valid iff the stack is empty.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Write a recursive factorial function and explain its recursion tree
records.problem_statement: Write a function factorial(n) using recursion that returns n!.
records.constraints_text: 0 \le n \le 20 (to fit standard 64-bit integer types). Time: O(n), Space: O(n) recursion stack.
records.solution_pseudocode: Function factorial(n): if n <= 1 return 1; otherwise return n * factorial(n-1).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Write a recursive Fibonacci function, then optimize it with memoization
records.problem_statement: Compute F(n) where F(0)=0, F(1)=1, F(n)=F(n-1)+F(n-2) using top-down recursive memoization.
records.constraints_text: 0 \le n \le 90. Time Complexity: O(n), Space: O(n).
records.solution_pseudocode: Function fib(n): if n <= 1 return n; otherwise return fib(n-1)+fib(n-2). Add a memo map so each fib(n) is computed once.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Generate all subsets (the power set) of an array
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use backtracking(index, current). At each index either include nums[index] or skip it. Record current at every recursion level.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the N-Queens problem using backtracking
records.problem_statement: Place N chess queens on an N \times N chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Return all distinct solutions.
records.solution_pseudocode: Place one queen per row. Try each column that is not blocked by a used column or diagonal, place the queen, recurse to the next row, then undo the choice.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve a Sudoku puzzle using backtracking
records.problem_statement: Write a program to solve a Sudoku puzzle (9 \times 9 grid) by filling the empty cells (represented by '.').
records.constraints_text: Grid size fixed at 9 \times 9. Guaranteed single unique solution.
records.solution_pseudocode: Find the next empty cell. Try digits 1..9 that are absent from its row, column and 3x3 box. Place one, recurse, and undo on failure. Stop when no empty cells remain.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all combinations of numbers that sum to a target (Combination Sum)
records.problem_statement: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer target, return a list of all unique combinations where chosen numbers sum to target. Same number can be chosen unlimited times.
records.solution_pseudocode: Backtrack with start index and remaining target. Choose each candidate at or after start, subtract it from target, recurse with the same index to allow reuse, then undo.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Generate all valid combinations of n pairs of balanced parentheses
records.problem_statement: Given n pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le n \le 8. Output size is the n^{\text{th}} Catalan number C_n.
records.solution_pseudocode: Push opening brackets onto a stack. For a closing bracket, verify the stack is non-empty and its top matches; otherwise return false. At the end the stack must be empty.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all paths from top-left to bottom-right of a grid, moving only right or down
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N grid, print or count all unique paths from (0,0) to (M-1, N-1) moving only right or down at any point.
records.solution_pseudocode: Backtrack from (0,0). Move right or down while inside the grid, append each cell to the current path, and record the path when reaching the bottom-right.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Rat in a Maze problem using backtracking
records.problem_statement: A rat starts at (0,0) in an N \times N matrix and needs to reach (N-1, N-1). 1 represents open cell, 0 represents blocked. Return all valid directions (D, L, R, U).
records.solution_pseudocode: At each cell, if it is inside the maze, open, and unvisited, mark it and recursively try valid directions. Unmark on return and record when the destination is reached.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print all letter combinations a phone keypad digit sequence can form
records.problem_statement: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent based on phone button mappings.
records.solution_pseudocode: Map each digit to its letters. Backtrack over digit positions, append each possible letter, recurse, then remove it. Record complete combinations.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve Tower of Hanoi and count the minimum number of moves
records.problem_statement: Write a recursive function to move N disks from source rod to destination rod using an auxiliary rod. Print moves and return total count (2^N - 1).
records.solution_pseudocode: To move n disks from source to target using auxiliary: move n-1 source->aux, move disk n source->target, then move n-1 aux->target. Total moves = 2^n - 1.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Compute x^n using recursion in O(log n) time (fast exponentiation)
records.problem_statement: Implement pow(x, n), which calculates x raised to the power n (x^n).
records.solution_pseudocode: If n is 0 return 1. Recursively compute half = power(x, floor(n/2)); square it. If n is odd multiply by x once more; handle negative n with reciprocal if required.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a word exists in a 2D letter grid via adjacent-cell paths (Word Search)
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid. Words can be constructed from sequentially adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically).
records.solution_pseudocode: DFS from every cell matching word[0]. Mark the cell visited, recursively match the next character in four directions, then unmark on backtracking.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Partition a string so every substring is a palindrome; return all such partitions
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, partition s such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Return all possible palindrome partitioning of s.
records.solution_pseudocode: Backtrack over substring end positions. Whenever s[start:end] is a palindrome, add it to the current partition, recurse from end, then remove it on return.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find two numbers that add up to a target using a hash map (Two Sum)
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, use a hash map to return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target in O(N) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a hash map from value to index. For each value x, compute target-x; if it exists return the pair, otherwise store x.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the first repeating element in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr of size N, find the first repeating element whose index of first occurrence is smallest.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^6, 0 \le arr[i] \le 10^6. Time: O(N), Space: O(N).
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan from left to right with a set. If an element already exists, return it; otherwise insert it into the set.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether two arrays contain the same elements, ignoring order and duplicates
records.problem_statement: Given two arrays A and B, check if both sets of elements are identical (i.e. set equality Set(A) == Set(B)).
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert distinct elements of each array into sets and compare the sets.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest subarray with sum zero using a hash map
records.problem_statement: Given an array arr containing positive and negative integers, find the length of the longest subarray with a sum equal to 0.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain prefixSum and a map from prefixSum to first index. When the same prefix sum appears again, the subarray between those indices has sum zero; maximize its length.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count the number of subarrays with sum equal to a given value k
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to k.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain running prefixSum and frequency map. For each position, add frequency[prefixSum - k] to the answer, then increment frequency[prefixSum].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all elements appearing more than n/k times in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an array of size N and an integer k, find all elements that appear more than \lfloor N/k \rfloor times.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use generalized Boyer-Moore with at most k-1 candidates. Make a candidate pass, then count each surviving candidate in a second pass and return those exceeding n/k.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Design a HashMap from scratch without using a built-in hash table
records.problem_statement: Design a HashMap without using any built-in hash table libraries. Support put(key, value), get(key), and remove(key) using separate chaining (linked list buckets).
records.solution_pseudocode: Create an array of buckets. Hash a key to a bucket index, then store key-value pairs in that bucket using a linked list or dynamic list. Implement put, get and remove with collision handling.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the shortest subarray that, if sorted, makes the whole array sorted
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, find the shortest unsorted continuous subarray such that if you only sort this subarray in ascending order, then the whole array will be sorted.
records.solution_pseudocode: Find first index where array decreases from left and last index where it decreases from right. Determine min/max inside that interval, then expand left/right while outside values violate the sorted order.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a subarray with a given sum exists in an array with positive and negative numbers
records.problem_statement: Given an array of positive and negative numbers and a target sum, return true if there exists a contiguous subarray with sum equal to target.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain a running prefix sum and a set of seen prefix sums. If prefixSum - target has been seen, a matching subarray exists; otherwise insert the current prefix sum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement inorder, preorder, and postorder traversal, recursively and iteratively
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder traversals both recursively and iteratively.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursive: visit left/root/right according to traversal order. Iterative: use a stack to simulate recursion; for inorder push left spine, for preorder process before pushing children, and for postorder use two stacks or state markers.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement level-order (BFS) traversal of a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e. level by level, left to right).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a queue initialized with root. Repeatedly pop a node, record it, and enqueue its non-null children.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum depth (height) of a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
records.solution_pseudocode: If root is null return 0. Recursively compute leftDepth and rightDepth and return 1 + max(leftDepth, rightDepth).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether two binary trees are structurally identical
records.problem_statement: Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, write a function to check if they are the same (structurally identical and node values equal).
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively compare corresponding nodes. Both null means true; one null or unequal values means false; otherwise compare left subtrees and right subtrees.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a binary tree is symmetric (a mirror of itself)
records.solution_pseudocode: Compare the tree with its mirror: recursively compare left of one node with right of the other and vice versa.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Invert (mirror) a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree (swap left and right subtrees for all nodes), and return its root.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively swap root.left and root.right, then invert both subtrees. Return root.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a binary tree is height-balanced
records.problem_statement: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced (where left and right subtrees of every node differ in height by no more than 1).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a recursive height function returning -1 when an imbalance is detected. Compute left/right heights; if their difference exceeds 1 return -1, otherwise return 1 + max(left,right).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the right-side view and left-side view of a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the values of nodes visible when looking at the tree from the Right and Left sides.
records.solution_pseudocode: Perform level-order traversal. For each level, record the first node for the left view and the last node for the right view.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the top view and bottom view of a binary tree (horizontal distance)
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, print the nodes visible when viewed from Top and Bottom (grouped by horizontal distance from root).
records.solution_pseudocode: BFS with horizontal distance. For each horizontal distance, record the first node seen for top view and continuously update the last node seen for bottom view.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the vertical order traversal of a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, calculate the vertical order traversal, ordered from top-to-bottom and left-to-right by vertical coordinates.
records.solution_pseudocode: BFS while storing horizontal distance and level. Group nodes by horizontal distance, preserving level order; sort/group according to the required vertical traversal rules.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the zigzag (spiral) level-order traversal of a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Return the zigzag level order traversal of nodes' values (i.e. left-to-right, then right-to-left for the next level).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a queue initialized with root. Repeatedly pop a node, record it, and enqueue its non-null children.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two nodes in a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes p and q.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [2, 10^5], all node values are unique.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively search left and right. If root is null or equals either target, return root. If both sides return non-null, root is the LCA; otherwise return the non-null side.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the LCA of two nodes in a Binary Search Tree
records.problem_statement: Given a BST and two nodes p and q, find their LCA using BST properties in O(H) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Start at root. If both targets are smaller move left; if both are larger move right; otherwise the current node is the LCA.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the diameter of a binary tree (longest path between any two nodes)
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter (the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree).
records.solution_pseudocode: Postorder-return subtree height. At each node, update diameter with leftHeight + rightHeight. Return 1 + max(leftHeight,rightHeight) to the parent.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum path sum between any two nodes in a binary tree
records.problem_statement: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes has an edge. Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.
records.solution_pseudocode: Postorder-return the best downward gain from each node. Clamp child gains at zero, update global answer with node.val + leftGain + rightGain, and return node.val + max(leftGain,rightGain).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a root-to-leaf path with a given sum exists (Path Sum)
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree and an integer targetSum, return true if the tree has a root-to-leaf path such that adding up all values along the path equals targetSum.
records.solution_pseudocode: DFS with remaining = target - node.val. At each leaf, return whether remaining equals zero; otherwise recurse into children.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print all root-to-leaf paths that sum to a target value (Path Sum II)
records.problem_statement: Return all root-to-leaf paths where each path's sum equals targetSum.
records.solution_pseudocode: DFS while appending node values to a current path and reducing the remaining sum. When a leaf reaches zero, copy the path into the result. Backtrack afterward.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the sum of all root-to-leaf numbers formed as digit paths
records.problem_statement: Each root-to-leaf path represents a number (e.g. 1 \to 2 \to 3 is 123). Return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.
records.solution_pseudocode: DFS carrying currentNumber = currentNumber*10 + node.val. At each leaf add currentNumber to the total.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Construct a binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversal sequences
records.problem_statement: Given two integer arrays preorder and inorder, construct and return the binary tree.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a map from inorder value to index. The next preorder value is the root; recursively build the left subtree from the left inorder range and the right subtree from the right range.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Convert a sorted array into a height-balanced Binary Search Tree
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums where the elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set low = 0 and high = n - 1. Repeatedly compute mid. If a[mid] equals target return it; if smaller search right half; otherwise search left half. For recursion, call the same logic on the selected half.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Flatten a binary tree into a linked list in place, following preorder
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, flatten the tree into a "linked list" using the right pointers, following preorder traversal order.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [0, 2000]. Space Complexity: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: For each node, recursively flatten left and right. Move the flattened left subtree to the right, attach the original right subtree after it, and set left to null.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Validate whether a given binary tree is a valid Binary Search Tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively enforce a valid numeric range. Each node must be strictly between low and high; recurse left with high=node.val and right with low=node.val.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the Kth smallest element in a BST using inorder traversal
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary search tree, and an integer k, return the k^{\text{th}} smallest value (1-indexed) of all the values of the nodes in the tree.
records.solution_pseudocode: Perform iterative inorder traversal. Decrement k when visiting a node; the node where k becomes zero is the kth smallest.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all nodes at distance K from a given node in a binary tree
records.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, a target node, and an integer k, return an array of the values of all nodes that have a distance k from the target node.
