records.solution_pseudocode: Build parent pointers with DFS/BFS, then BFS outward from the target node while tracking distance and visited nodes. Collect nodes when distance equals k.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize it back to the same tree
records.problem_statement: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize that string back to the original tree structure.
records.solution_pseudocode: Serialize using preorder with a null marker. Deserialize by consuming tokens in order: create a node for a value and recursively build its left and right children; return null for the marker.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement graph representations using an adjacency list and adjacency matrix
records.problem_statement: Write data structures to represent an undirected/directed graph with V vertices and E edges using Adjacency List and Adjacency Matrix.
records.solution_pseudocode: For an adjacency list, create a list for each vertex and add each edge to the appropriate list. For an adjacency matrix, initialize an NxN matrix and set matrix[u][v] according to each edge.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal of a graph
records.problem_statement: Given a connected undirected graph represented as an adjacency list and a starting vertex S, return the BFS traversal sequence.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize a queue with the start vertex and mark it visited. Repeatedly dequeue, record, and enqueue every unvisited neighbor.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal of a graph
records.problem_statement: Given a connected undirected graph, return the DFS traversal sequence starting from node 0.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use recursion or an explicit stack. Mark a vertex visited when first seen, then recursively/iteratively process each unvisited neighbor.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Detect a cycle in an undirected graph using BFS or DFS
records.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph with V vertices and E edges, return true if the graph contains any cycle, else false.
records.solution_pseudocode: Run BFS/DFS while tracking each node parent. When an already visited neighbor is found that is not the current node parent, a cycle exists.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Detect a cycle in a directed graph using DFS
records.problem_statement: Given a directed graph with V vertices and E edges, determine whether it contains a cycle (using visited and recursion stack states).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DFS with three states: unvisited, visiting, visited. An edge to a visiting node is a back edge, so a cycle exists.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Given a grid of 0s and 1s, count the number of islands (connected components)
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N 2D binary grid grid where '1' represents land and '0' represents water, return the number of islands (connected 4-directionally).
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan the grid. When a cell is 1, increment island count and BFS/DFS from it, turning all connected 1s into 0 or marking them visited.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Perform a topological sort on a Directed Acyclic Graph
records.problem_statement: Given a DAG with V vertices and E edges, return a linear ordering of vertices such that for every directed edge U \to V, vertex U comes before V.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute indegree of every vertex. Push all indegree-zero vertices into a queue and repeatedly remove one, decrement neighbors, and enqueue neighbors whose indegree becomes zero.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a graph is bipartite
records.problem_statement: Given an undirected graph, return true if it is bipartite (nodes can be partitioned into 2 sets such that every edge connects set A and set B).
records.solution_pseudocode: Color each connected component with two colors using BFS/DFS. For every edge, neighboring vertices must have opposite colors; a conflict means not bipartite.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the shortest path in an unweighted graph using BFS
records.problem_statement: Given an unweighted graph, find the shortest distance (number of edges) from a source node S to all other nodes.
records.solution_pseudocode: BFS from the source. Store distance when a vertex is first discovered. The first time the destination is reached gives the shortest distance.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm for shortest paths in a weighted graph
records.problem_statement: Given a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights and a source vertex S, compute the shortest path distance to all vertices.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize dist[source]=0 and all others infinity. Repeatedly extract the minimum-distance vertex from a min-heap and relax each outgoing edge, pushing improved distances back into the heap.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Bellman–Ford and explain how it handles negative edge weights
records.problem_statement: Find single-source shortest paths in a directed graph with negative weights, and detect if a negative weight cycle exists.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize source distance to 0. Repeat V-1 times: relax every edge u->v. If no distance changes, stop early. One more pass detects a negative cycle.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Kruskal's algorithm for a Minimum Spanning Tree using Union-Find
records.problem_statement: Given a connected, undirected, weighted graph, find the sum of edge weights in its Minimum Spanning Tree using Kruskal's greedy algorithm.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort all edges by weight. Initialize DSU. For each edge in order, if endpoints are in different sets, union them and add the edge to the MST.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Prim's algorithm for a Minimum Spanning Tree
records.problem_statement: Find the total weight of the Minimum Spanning Tree of a graph using Prim's algorithm with a priority queue.
records.solution_pseudocode: Start from any vertex, push its outgoing edges into a min-heap, and repeatedly take the cheapest edge leading to an unvisited vertex; add the edge and push the new vertex edges.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) with path compression and union by rank
records.problem_statement: Design a DSU data structure supporting find(i) and union(i, j) in near-constant time O(\alpha(N)).
records.solution_pseudocode: Store parent and rank/size arrays. find(x) follows parents and compresses paths. union(a,b) attaches the smaller-rank root below the larger-rank root.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Clone a graph, given a reference to one node in a connected undirected graph
records.problem_statement: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a map from original node to cloned node. DFS/BFS each original node once, create its clone, then recursively clone and attach every neighbor.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Determine whether a course schedule with prerequisites is completable
records.problem_statement: There are numCourses courses you have to take (0 to numCourses-1). Given prerequisites [a, b] (b \to a), return true if you can finish all courses.
records.solution_pseudocode: Build a directed prerequisite graph and indegree counts. Run Kahn topological sorting; if all courses are processed, the schedule is completable.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the number of provinces (connected components) given a friendship matrix
records.problem_statement: There are N cities. If city A is connected to city B, they form a province. Given an N \times N matrix isConnected, return total provinces.
records.solution_pseudocode: Treat the matrix as a graph. Run DFS/BFS from every unvisited city and increment the component count each time a new traversal starts.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Rot all oranges in a grid in minimum time, given spread rules (multi-source BFS)
records.problem_statement: You are given an M \times N grid where 0=\text{empty}, 1=\text{fresh orange}, 2=\text{rotten orange}. Return minimum minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Put all initially rotten oranges into a queue with time 0. Process them level by level, turning adjacent fresh oranges rotten and recording time. The maximum time is the answer; if fresh oranges remain, return failure.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the shortest path from source to destination in a binary maze/grid
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N binary matrix, find the shortest path length from top-left to bottom-right passing only through 0s.
records.solution_pseudocode: BFS from the source over cells containing 0/open space. Track distance for each cell; return the distance when destination is first reached.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all bridges (critical connections) in a graph
records.problem_statement: A critical connection is an edge that, if removed, will make the graph disconnected. Return all critical connections using Tarjan's algorithm.
records.solution_pseudocode: Run DFS with discovery time and low-link value. For tree edge u-v, after DFS(v), if low[v] > disc[u], the edge u-v is a bridge.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all articulation points (cut vertices) in a graph
records.problem_statement: An articulation point is a vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components. Find all cut vertices using DFS discovery times.
records.solution_pseudocode: Run DFS with discovery and low times. A non-root u is an articulation point if some child v has low[v] >= disc[u]. The root is one when it has more than one DFS child.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find strongly connected components in a directed graph (Kosaraju's or Tarjan's algorithm)
records.problem_statement: Given a directed graph, print/count all Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) where every vertex is reachable from every other vertex in the component.
records.solution_pseudocode: Kosaraju: DFS the original graph to build a finish-order stack, reverse all edges, then DFS in reverse finish order; each traversal yields one SCC.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement Floyd–Warshall for all-pairs shortest paths
records.problem_statement: Given a weighted graph, compute the shortest distance between every pair of vertices.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize dist[i][j] with edge weights and zero diagonals. For each intermediate k, update dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Given flight routes with costs, find the cheapest path with at most k stops
records.problem_statement: There are n cities connected by flights with costs. Given src, dst, k, find the cheapest price from src to dst with at most k stops.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use dynamic programming for at most k+1 edges: keep the best cost to each city, relax all flights once per stop, and use a copy of the previous layer so one iteration adds at most one edge.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of swaps needed to sort an array, modeled as a graph problem
records.problem_statement: Given an array of N distinct elements, find the minimum number of swaps required to sort the array.
records.solution_pseudocode: Map each value to its sorted target index. Build permutation cycles; a cycle of length L needs L-1 swaps. Sum over all cycles.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the Nth Fibonacci number using bottom-up tabulation
records.problem_statement: Compute F(N) using an array table in O(N) time and O(1) space.
records.solution_pseudocode: If n is 0 return 0. Keep prev2=0 and prev1=1. Repeat from 2 to n: cur=prev1+prev2; shift the two variables. Return prev1.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Climbing Stairs problem (count distinct ways to reach the top)
records.problem_statement: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways.
records.solution_pseudocode: Let dp[0]=1 and dp[1]=1. For i from 2..n, dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Return dp[n].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the 0/1 Knapsack problem
records.problem_statement: Given weights and values of N items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get the maximum total value. Each item can be picked at most once.
records.solution_pseudocode: Create dp[capacity+1] initialized to zero. For each item, iterate capacity from W down to weight[i]; update dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c-weight[i]] + value[i]).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Coin Change problem (minimum coins to make a value)
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array coins and an integer amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount. Return -1 if impossible.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set dp[0]=0 and all other dp amounts to infinity. For each amount, test every coin and use dp[amount] = min(dp[amount], dp[amount-coin] + 1) when the coin fits.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count the number of ways to make a value using unlimited coin denominations
records.problem_statement: Given coins array and an integer amount, return the number of combinations that make up that amount.
records.solution_pseudocode: Set dp[0]=1. For each coin, iterate amounts from coin to target and add dp[amount-coin] into dp[amount]. Return dp[target].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in O(N \log N) or O(N^2) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain tails where tails[len-1] is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length len. For each value, binary-search its insertion position and replace there. Return tails size.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum edits to convert one string into another (Edit Distance)
records.problem_statement: Compute minimum insertion, deletion, and replacement operations to transform string A to B using dynamic programming.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the minimum edits to transform the first i characters of A into the first j of B. Match characters diagonally; otherwise take 1 + min(delete, insert, replace).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Matrix Chain Multiplication problem (minimum multiplication cost)
records.problem_statement: Given a sequence of matrices, find the most efficient way to multiply these matrices together (minimum scalar multiplications).
records.constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 100, where matrix dimensions array size is N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Let dp[i][j] be the minimum scalar multiplications for matrices i..j. Try every split k and update dp[i][j] with left cost + right cost + multiplication cost. Return dp[1][n].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum sum of non-adjacent elements in an array (House Robber)
records.problem_statement: You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has money, but adjacent houses have security systems connected. Return max money.
records.solution_pseudocode: Keep prev2 and prev1. For each house x, current = max(prev1, prev2 + x); shift prev2=prev1 and prev1=current. Return prev1.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum path sum from top-left to bottom-right of a grid
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from top-left to bottom-right which minimizes the sum of all numbers along its path.
records.solution_pseudocode: Fill a DP grid where dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]), using proper boundary initialization. Return dp[m-1][n-1].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count unique paths from top-left to bottom-right of a grid with obstacles
records.problem_statement: An M \times N grid contains obstacles (1). Count unique paths from (0,0) to (M-1, N-1) moving only right or down.
records.solution_pseudocode: Backtrack from (0,0). Move right or down while inside the grid, append each cell to the current path, and record the path when reaching the bottom-right.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Determine whether a set can be split into two subsets of equal sum
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of elements in both subsets is equal.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute total sum; if odd return false. Use 0/1 subset-sum DP to determine whether sum/2 can be formed.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum profit from a single buy/sell of a stock over given daily prices
records.subtopic_name: Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock I
records.problem_statement: Given array prices where prices[i] is price on day i, maximize profit by choosing a single day to buy and a future day to sell.
records.solution_pseudocode: Track the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit. For each price, update profit with price-minPrice, then update minPrice.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum profit from unlimited buy/sell transactions on a stock
records.subtopic_name: Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock II
records.problem_statement: You may complete as many transactions as you like (i.e., buy one and sell one share of the stock multiple times). Find max profit.
records.solution_pseudocode: For each day after the first, add max(0, prices[i]-prices[i-1]) to profit.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum profit from stock trading with at most two transactions
records.subtopic_name: Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock III
records.problem_statement: Find the maximum profit you can achieve given stock prices array with at most two transactions.
records.solution_pseudocode: Track four states: best after first buy, first sell, second buy, second sell. Update them for each price in that order and return second-sell.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest palindromic subsequence in a string using DP
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence in s.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use interval DP. For single characters dp[i][i]=1. For increasing lengths, if s[i]==s[j], use inner length + 2; otherwise take max of excluding either end.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve Word Break using DP (check if a string segments into dictionary words)
records.problem_statement: Use dynamic programming table to determine if string s can be formed by concatenating words from dictionary wordDict.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use dp[i] = true when prefix s[0:i] can be segmented. For each i, test every prior split j and set dp[i] if dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is in the dictionary.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the number of ways to decode a numeric string into letters (Decode Ways)
records.problem_statement: Given a string s containing digits, return the number of ways to decode it where 'A' -> 1, ..., 'Z' -> 26.
records.solution_pseudocode: Let dp[i] be ways to decode the first i characters. Add dp[i-1] when the current digit is non-zero; add dp[i-2] when the last two digits form 10..26.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the largest square of all 1s in a binary matrix (Maximal Square)
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N binary matrix filled with 0's and 1's, find the largest square containing only 1's and return its area.
records.solution_pseudocode: For each cell containing 1, dp[i][j] = 1 + min(top, left, diagonal). Track the largest side and return side squared.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Egg Dropping puzzle (minimum trials to find the critical floor)
records.problem_statement: You have K eggs and a building with N floors. Find the minimum number of moves required to determine with certainty the highest floor from which an egg can be dropped without breaking.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP over eggs and floors, trying each dropping floor and taking 1 + max(brokenCase, notBrokenCase); optimize with binary search or moves-based DP when desired.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of an array using DP
records.problem_statement: Compute minimum jumps to reach last index using 1D DP array DP[i] = 1 + \min(DP[j]).
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize dp[0]=0 and others infinity. For each index i, update every reachable j in i+1..i+nums[i] with dp[j] = min(dp[j], dp[i]+1). Return dp[n-1].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the Rod Cutting problem (maximize revenue from cutting a rod)
records.problem_statement: Given a rod of length N and an array of prices that includes prices of all pieces of size smaller than N, determine the maximum value obtainable by cutting up the rod and selling the pieces.
records.solution_pseudocode: Let dp[len] be maximum value for a rod of length len. For every len, try each first cut c and maximize price[c] + dp[len-c].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count the number of Boolean parenthesizations that evaluate to true
records.problem_statement: Given a boolean expression of operands (T, F) and operators (&, |, ^), count the number of ways to parenthesize the expression so that it evaluates to true.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use interval DP storing trueWays[i][j] and falseWays[i][j]. For each operator split, combine left/right true/false counts according to &, |, ^. Return trueWays for the full expression.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest common substring (not subsequence) of two strings
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, find the length of the longest common continuous substring.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the length of the common suffix ending at s1[i-1], s2[j-1]. If equal, dp = diagonal + 1; otherwise zero. Track the maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve Activity Selection (maximum non-overlapping activities)
records.problem_statement: Given N activities with start and finish times, select the maximum number of activities that can be performed by a single person (non-overlapping).
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort activities by finish time. Select the first one, then repeatedly choose the next activity whose start is at least the last selected finish.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve the fractional Knapsack problem greedily
records.problem_statement: Given weights and values of N items and knapsack capacity W, calculate maximum total value where items can be broken into smaller fractions.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute value/weight for every item, sort descending by ratio, then take as much as possible from each item until capacity is full.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum coins for a value greedily, and explain when greedy fails
records.problem_statement: Given canonical coin denominations \\{1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 2000\\} and target amount V, find minimum coins needed using greedy approach.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort coin denominations descending. Take as many of the largest coin as possible, then continue with smaller coins. Greedy is correct for canonical coin systems but can fail for arbitrary denominations.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Solve Job Sequencing to maximize profit within deadlines
records.problem_statement: Given a set of N jobs where each job i has a deadline and profit, find maximum profit earned if only one job can be scheduled at a time unit.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort jobs by descending profit. For each job, place it in the latest available slot on or before its deadline; skip it when no slot exists.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of meeting rooms required for a list of intervals
records.problem_statement: Given an array of meeting time intervals consisting of start and end times [start_i, end_i], find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort start times and end times separately. Use two pointers; when a meeting starts before the earliest ending meeting, increment room count, otherwise decrement it. Track the maximum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Construct a Huffman encoding for a set of characters and frequencies
records.problem_statement: Given N characters and their frequencies, construct a Huffman tree and print prefix-free binary codes for each character.
records.solution_pseudocode: Push all characters with frequencies into a min-heap. Repeatedly remove the two least frequent nodes, merge them, and reinsert. Traverse the final tree to assign 0/1 codes.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Distribute candies satisfying rating-based constraints with minimum total candies
records.problem_statement: There are N children standing in a line with ratings. Each child must get at least 1 candy. Children with a higher rating than neighbors get more candies.
records.solution_pseudocode: Give every child one candy. Scan left-to-right increasing runs and right-to-left decreasing runs; each child gets max(left requirement, right requirement). Sum the candies.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the minimum number of refueling stops to reach a destination (gas station problem)
records.problem_statement: A car starts with startFuel gas. Stations are located along the route. Find minimum refueling stops to reach target distance using Max-Heap.
records.solution_pseudocode: Process stations reachable with the current fuel and push their fuel amounts into a max-heap. When fuel is insufficient to reach the next station, refuel using the largest available amount; count stops.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a Min-Heap and a Max-Heap from scratch, with insert and extract operations
records.problem_statement: Design custom Min-Heap and Max-Heap classes supporting insert(x), extractMin() / extractMax(), and heapify() operations using array storage.
records.solution_pseudocode: Represent each heap in an array. Insert by appending and bubbling upward while the heap property is violated. Extract-root by swapping with the last item, shrinking the heap, and heapifying downward; reverse the comparison for max-heap.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the K closest points to the origin from a list of points
records.problem_statement: Given an array of points (x,y) on 2D plane and integer K, return K closest points to origin (0,0) based on Euclidean distance.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain a max-heap of size k using squared distance x*x+y*y. For each point push it; if heap size exceeds k, remove the farthest point.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Merge K sorted linked lists using a min-heap
records.problem_statement: You are given an array of K linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted list.
records.constraints_text: 0 \le K \le 10^4, total nodes \le 10^4. Time: O(N \log K).
records.solution_pseudocode: Push the head of each non-empty list into a min-heap keyed by node value. Repeatedly extract the smallest node, append it to the result, and push its next node.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the running median of a stream of numbers using two heaps
records.problem_statement: Design a data structure that supports adding numbers from a data stream and finding the current median in O(1) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain max-heap left and min-heap right. Insert each value into the appropriate heap and rebalance their sizes so they differ by at most one. The median comes from the top(s).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the top K frequent elements in an array
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.
records.constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, -10^4 \le nums[i] \le 10^4, 1 \le k \le \text{number of unique elements}.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count frequencies with a hash map. Keep a min-heap of size k keyed by frequency. Push each entry and remove the smallest when the heap grows beyond k.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a priority-queue-based task scheduler with cooldown constraints
records.problem_statement: Given CPU tasks represented by characters and a cooldown integer n, return minimum units of time required to finish all tasks.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count task frequencies. Use a max-heap for available tasks and a queue for tasks waiting until their cooldown ends. At each time unit schedule the most frequent available task or idle.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Connect n ropes with minimum total cost, given their lengths, using a min-heap
records.problem_statement: Given N ropes of different lengths, connect them into one rope. Cost to connect two ropes is equal to sum of their lengths. Minimize total cost.
records.solution_pseudocode: Push all rope lengths into a min-heap. Repeatedly pop the two smallest, add their sum to total cost, and push the combined rope back.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a given array represents a valid Min-Heap
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers arr, determine if it represents a complete binary tree that satisfies the Min-Heap property (parent \le children).
records.solution_pseudocode: For every index i with children, verify parent[i] <= each child. If all checks pass, the array is a valid min-heap.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check whether a number is a power of two using bit manipulation
records.problem_statement: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two (n > 0 and (n \& (n-1)) == 0).
records.solution_pseudocode: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Return n > 0 and (n & (n-1)) == 0.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count the number of set bits (1s) in a number's binary representation
records.problem_statement: Write a function that takes an unsigned integer and returns the number of '1' bits it has (Hamming weight).
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n is not zero, add n & 1 to count and shift n right by one. Return count.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Swap two numbers without using a temporary variable
records.problem_statement: Given two variables a and b, swap their values using bitwise XOR operations without extra memory.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use XOR swapping: a = a XOR b; b = a XOR b; a = a XOR b. Do not use the method when both variables refer to the same storage location.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the two non-repeating numbers in an array where every other number appears twice
records.problem_statement: An array contains elements where all numbers appear twice except two numbers which appear once. Find those two unique numbers.
records.constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 10^5, -10^9 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
records.solution_pseudocode: XOR all elements to get x = a XOR b. Find any set bit in x to split numbers into two groups, then XOR each group separately to recover a and b.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check, set, clear, and toggle the ith bit of a number
records.problem_statement: Write functions to check if i^{\text{th}} bit is set, set i^{\text{th}} bit to 1, clear i^{\text{th}} bit to 0, and toggle i^{\text{th}} bit of integer N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Check with (n AND 1<<i), set with n OR 1<<i, clear with n AND NOT(1<<i), and toggle with n XOR 1<<i.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the position of the rightmost set bit in a number
records.problem_statement: Given an integer N, return the 1-based position of the rightmost set bit in its binary representation. If no set bit, return 0.
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute isolated = n AND (-n). The bit position of isolated is the rightmost set bit.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Multiply two numbers without the multiplication operator, using bit shifts
records.problem_statement: Given two positive integers a and b, calculate a \times b using only bitwise left shift, right shift, and addition.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use binary multiplication: while multiplier > 0, add the current multiplicand when the low bit is set, double the multiplicand, and shift the multiplier right.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement a Trie (prefix tree) with insert, search, and startsWith operations
records.problem_statement: Implement Trie class with insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix) methods.
records.solution_pseudocode: Each node stores children and an end-of-word flag. Insert follows/creates child nodes per character; search follows children and checks the end flag; prefix search only requires the path to exist.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find all dictionary words that can be formed on a letter board using a Trie + DFS (Word Search II)
records.problem_statement: Given an M \times N board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words present on the board.
records.solution_pseudocode: Build a Trie from the dictionary. DFS from each board cell, following Trie edges, marking cells visited and recording words when a terminal Trie node is reached; backtrack after each move.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Implement autocomplete suggestions for a given prefix using a Trie
records.problem_statement: Given a list of dictionary words and a search prefix, return all words in the dictionary that start with the prefix in alphabetical order.
records.solution_pseudocode: Traverse the Trie along the prefix. If the path exists, DFS from that node to collect complete words, stopping after the required number of suggestions.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the longest word in a dictionary buildable one character at a time, using a Trie
records.problem_statement: Given array of strings words, find the longest string in words that can be built one character at a time by other words in words.
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert all words into a set or Trie. Check words in increasing length; a word is buildable when every prefix obtained by removing the last character exists. Track the longest valid word.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find the maximum XOR of two numbers in an array using a bitwise Trie
records.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return the maximum result of nums[i] \oplus nums[j] where 0 \le i \le j < N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Insert binary representations into a bitwise Trie. For each number, greedily choose the opposite bit at every position to maximize XOR, and track the best value.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse a string
records.problem_statement: Write a function that reverses a string passed as a character array or string in-place.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use two pointers at the ends of the character array, swap characters, and move inward until the pointers meet.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Number is palindrome
records.problem_statement: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome integer, and false otherwise.
records.solution_pseudocode: Store the original number. Rebuild its reverse by repeatedly taking the last digit. Compare the reversed number with the original.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Binary to decimal
records.problem_statement: Convert a binary string or binary representation into its equivalent base-10 integer.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize value=0. For each binary digit d, update value = value*2 + d. Return value.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count vowels in string
records.problem_statement: Given a string s, count the total number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) present in it.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. Scan characters and increment count when the lowercased character is one of a, e, i, o, u.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check prime number
records.problem_statement: Given a number N, determine whether it is a prime number.
records.solution_pseudocode: Start from any vertex, push its outgoing edges into a min-heap, and repeatedly take the cheapest edge leading to an unvisited vertex; add the edge and push the new vertex edges.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Check Armstrong number
records.problem_statement: An Armstrong number of K digits is a number equal to sum of K^{\text{th}} power of its digits. Check if given N is Armstrong.
records.solution_pseudocode: Count the digits. Raise each digit to that digit-count, sum the powers, and compare the sum with the original number.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: GCD of two numbers
records.problem_statement: Compute Greatest Common Divisor of two integers a and b using Euclidean Algorithm.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use Euclid: while b is not zero, set (a,b) = (b, a mod b). Return a.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find LCM
records.problem_statement: Find Least Common Multiple of two integers a and b using formula \text{LCM}(a,b) = (a \times b) / \text{GCD}(a,b).
records.solution_pseudocode: Compute g = gcd(a,b). Return abs(a/g*b).

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count occurrence of elements
records.problem_statement: Given an array and a target element X, count how many times X appears in the array.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a frequency map. For each element increment its count, then return the map or requested frequencies.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: String to title case
records.problem_statement: Convert input string s to Title Case where the first letter of each word is capitalized and rest are lowercase.
records.solution_pseudocode: Split the string into words. For each word, uppercase the first character and lowercase the remaining characters, then join the words.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Missing and repeating number
records.problem_statement: Given unsorted array of size N containing elements from 1 to N. One number from 1..N is missing and one appears twice. Find both.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a frequency array or marking method. The value with count 2 is repeating; the value with count 0 is missing.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Number of digits in an integer
records.problem_statement: Given an integer N, count the total number of digits present in N.
records.constraints_text: -2^{31} \le N \le 2^{31}-1. Time Complexity: O(1) using \lfloor \log\_{10} N \rfloor + 1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Handle zero as one digit. Otherwise repeatedly divide the absolute number by 10 and count iterations.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Armstrong numbers in range
records.problem_statement: Given two integers low and high, print all Armstrong numbers in the range [low, high].
records.solution_pseudocode: For each number in the range, apply the Armstrong-number test and output numbers whose digit-power sum equals the number.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Array elements sum
records.problem_statement: Given an array of integers, compute total sum of all elements.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize total=0 and add every array element to total. Return total.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Factorial through loop
records.problem_statement: Compute factorial of N using an iterative loop.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize result=1. Multiply result by every integer from 2 through n. Return result.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Two numbers without temp swapping
records.problem_statement: Swap values of a and b using arithmetic operators (a = a+b; b = a-b; a = a-b).
records.solution_pseudocode: Swap the two values without a temporary variable using XOR: a=a XOR b; b=a XOR b; a=a XOR b.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Linear search
records.problem_statement: Search for element X in array of size N. Return first index or -1.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan from left to right. Return the index of the first element equal to target; return -1 if target is absent.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Add two matrices
records.problem_statement: Given two M \times N matrices A and B, compute matrix C = A + B.
records.solution_pseudocode: Create a result matrix of the same dimensions. For each cell, result[i][j] = A[i][j] + B[i][j].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print prime numbers within a range
records.problem_statement: Given range [L, R], print all prime numbers in the range using Sieve of Eratosthenes.
records.solution_pseudocode: Start from any vertex, push its outgoing edges into a min-heap, and repeatedly take the cheapest edge leading to an unvisited vertex; add the edge and push the new vertex edges.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print pattern of stars
records.problem_statement: Print standard pyramid star pattern for N rows.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use nested loops. The outer loop controls the row and the inner loop prints the required number of stars/spaces for that row according to the pattern.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Words in sentence count
records.problem_statement: Count the number of words in a given string sentence.
records.solution_pseudocode: Trim the sentence, split on whitespace, and count non-empty tokens.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Leap year check
records.problem_statement: Given year Y, determine if it is a leap year (divisible by 4 and not 100, unless divisible by 400).
records.solution_pseudocode: A year is leap if divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. Return the corresponding boolean.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Duplicates in array remove
records.problem_statement: Remove duplicate elements from an unsorted array while maintaining unique elements.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a set to track seen values. Add each unseen value to the result and skip values already present.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Remove white spaces from string
records.problem_statement: Remove all spaces from a given string in-place.
records.solution_pseudocode: Scan all characters and append only characters that are not whitespace to the result.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Sum of digits of a number
records.problem_statement: Calculate the sum of all digits of a given integer N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize sum=0. Repeatedly add n mod 10 and divide n by 10 until n becomes zero.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find median of array
records.problem_statement: Find the median element of an array after sorting.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sort the array. If length is odd return the middle value; otherwise return the average of the two middle values.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count set bits in integer
records.problem_statement: Count total 1s in binary representation of N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n is not zero, set n = n AND (n-1) and increment count. Return count.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Transpose of matrix
records.problem_statement: Given M \times N matrix A, return its transpose matrix A^T of size N \times M.
records.solution_pseudocode: Create a transposed matrix T where T[j][i] = A[i][j], or swap A[i][j] with A[j][i] above the diagonal for an in-place square matrix.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Calculate power with bitwise
records.problem_statement: Compute a^b using bitwise right shift to check odd/even powers in O(\log b) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use exponentiation by squaring: while exponent > 0, multiply result when the low bit is set, square the base, then shift exponent right.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Merge two strings alternatively
records.problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, merge them by adding letters in alternating order.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use two indices and append one character from each string alternately until one string ends, then append the remainder.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find duplicate elements
records.problem_statement: Find all elements that appear more than once in an array.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a set to track seen values. Add each unseen value to the result and skip values already present.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Diagonal sum of matrix
records.problem_statement: Compute the sum of primary and secondary diagonals of an N \times N square matrix.
records.solution_pseudocode: Sum matrix[i][i] for the main diagonal and matrix[i][n-1-i] for the secondary diagonal. Avoid double-counting the center if n is odd.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Subset sum problem
records.problem_statement: Given a set of non-negative integers and a value sum, determine if there is a subset with sum equal to sum.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use boolean DP where dp[s] indicates whether sum s is achievable. For each number, update sums from target down to number. Return dp[target].

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Print boundary of binary tree
records.problem_statement: Return boundary nodes of a binary tree anti-clockwise starting from root.
records.solution_pseudocode: Add root, then traverse the left boundary excluding leaves, collect all leaves left-to-right, then traverse the right boundary excluding leaves bottom-to-top.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Reverse stack recursively
records.problem_statement: Reverse a stack using recursion without extra helper stack structures.
records.solution_pseudocode: Recursively pop the top until the stack is empty. Then insert each popped element at the bottom using another recursive function.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Queue using linked list
records.problem_statement: Implement FIFO Queue using singly linked list nodes with enqueue and dequeue.
records.solution_pseudocode: Maintain front and rear node pointers. Enqueue by attaching a new node at rear; dequeue by removing front and updating front/rear when the queue becomes empty.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Binary tree to DLL
records.problem_statement: Convert a binary tree to a Doubly Linked List in-place following inorder traversal sequence.
records.solution_pseudocode: Perform inorder traversal. Link the current node with the previously visited node using left=prev and prev.right=current; update prev each time.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Heap sort
records.problem_statement: Implement Heap Sort algorithm using max heap building and repeated extraction.
records.solution_pseudocode: Build a max-heap. Repeatedly swap the root with the last unsorted element, reduce heap size, and heapify the root. The array becomes sorted.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Celebrity problem using stack
records.problem_statement: A celebrity is known to everyone but knows no one. Find celebrity in N people given matrix M[i][j] in O(N) time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Push all people onto a stack. Pop two at a time and discard anyone who cannot be the celebrity based on knows relation. Verify the final candidate knows nobody and everyone knows the candidate.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count set bits using Brian Kernighan's algo
records.problem_statement: Count set bits in N by repeatedly clearing rightmost set bit (N = N \& (N-1)).
records.solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n != 0, set n = n AND (n-1) and increment count. The number of iterations equals the number of set bits.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Maximum sum path in matrix
records.problem_statement: Find maximum path sum starting from any cell in top row to any cell in bottom row, moving down, down-left, down-right.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP from the top row. For each cell, add its value to the maximum of allowed predecessor cells (up/diagonals or according to the problem definition). Track the maximum in the last row.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Snake and ladder game simulation
records.problem_statement: Given board configuration with snakes and ladders, find minimum dice throws to reach destination square 100 using BFS.
records.constraints_text: Board size 100 cells, up to 30 snakes/ladders.
records.solution_pseudocode: Model board cells as graph edges from each position to up to six next dice positions, applying snakes/ladders. BFS from start gives the minimum number of dice throws.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count number of BSTs
records.problem_statement: Given N nodes, count total unique BSTs that can be formed using N^{\text{th}} Catalan number C_N.
records.solution_pseudocode: Let dp[n] be the number of unique BSTs with n nodes. dp[0]=dp[1]=1. For each n, sum dp[left]*dp[right] over every possible root.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Inorder successor in BST
records.problem_statement: Find the in-order successor of a given node P in a Binary Search Tree.
records.constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 10^4]. Time: O(H).
records.solution_pseudocode: If node has a right subtree, return its leftmost node. Otherwise walk from the root, moving left when current value is greater than target and remembering that node as successor.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Count distinct subsequences
records.problem_statement: Given a string S, count number of distinct non-empty subsequences modulo 10^9+7.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use DP over prefixes. For each character c, newCount = 2*dp + 1 minus the number of subsequences previously ending with c. Track last contribution for each character modulo the required modulus.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Word ladder
records.problem_statement: Given two words beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return shortest transformation sequence length changing 1 letter at a time.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use BFS from beginWord. Generate all one-letter mutations that exist in the dictionary, remove visited words, and continue level by level until endWord is found.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Evaluation of expression tree
records.problem_statement: Given a binary expression tree where leaves are values and internal nodes are operators, evaluate total expression value.
records.solution_pseudocode: Postorder recursively evaluate children. If the node is a value return it; otherwise apply the operator to the evaluated left and right results.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Bit manipulation problems
records.problem_statement: Practice utility functions for single number detection, bit flips required to convert number A to B, and swap nibbles.
records.solution_pseudocode: Single number: XOR all values. Bit flips A to B: count set bits in A XOR B. Swap nibbles: extract low/high 4-bit groups and exchange their positions.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Number of smaller elements to right
records.problem_statement: Given array nums, return an array counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i] (using Merge Sort or Segment Tree).
records.solution_pseudocode: Use merge sort on indexed values. During merge, when taking a right-half value before a left-half value, add the number of remaining smaller right elements to the left index count.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Burst balloons problem
records.problem_statement: Given N balloons with coins, burst all balloons to maximize total coins collected using interval DP.
records.solution_pseudocode: Add virtual balloons with value 1 at both ends. Use interval DP: choose the last balloon to burst inside each interval and maximize leftDP + value*neighbor values + rightDP.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Max points from cards
records.problem_statement: There are N cards in a row. In one step, take 1 card from beginning or end. Maximize score after taking exactly K cards.
records.solution_pseudocode: Take x cards from the left and k-x from the right for every x from 0..k. Track the maximum combined sum, or equivalently minimize the sum of the middle n-k cards.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Find centroid of a tree
records.problem_statement: Find a node in a tree such that removing it leaves no connected component with size greater than N/2.
records.solution_pseudocode: Run DFS to compute subtree sizes. A node is a centroid when every remaining component after removing it has size <= n/2. Return such a node.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Convert BST to greater sum tree
records.problem_statement: Transform a BST such that every key is changed to original key plus sum of all keys greater than original key in BST.
records.solution_pseudocode: Traverse the BST in reverse inorder (right, root, left) while maintaining a running sum of greater values. Replace each node value with node.value + runningSum before updating the running sum.

records.source_notes: User-provided coding question bank
records.title: Longest valid parentheses
records.problem_statement: Given a string containing just '(' and ')', find the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.
records.solution_pseudocode: Use a stack of indices initialized with -1. Push the index of each opening parenthesis. For a closing parenthesis, pop; if the stack becomes empty push the current index, otherwise update maximum length as i - stack.top.
